designationHistory.indexText: Established in 1959 when Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act lands at War Horse Lake, Wild Horse Lake and Yellow Water Reservoir were transferred to the Fish and Wildlife Service for waterfowl.

authority.citation: Transfer of Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act lands

designationHistory.note: The refuge page gives only the month or year.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: War Horse National Wildlife Refuge, About Us

FWS news release, Nov. 20, 1959: transfer of jurisdiction over 3,200 acres in the War Horse Lake, Wild Horse Lake and Yellow Water Reservoir areas, Petroleum County, to form "a new haven" for waterfowl

designationHistory.indexOriginal: War Horse NWR was not established by a specific executive order, but through a transfer of lands by the authority of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act in 1959.
